mainTopic: מוקצה cases from the משנה: a child holding a stone, a basket with a stone, moving impure תרומה (לצורך גופו vs. לצורך מקומו), and רבי יהודה's ruling on lifting nullified תרומה
overview: The amud opens by explaining why a child holding a stone may be lifted but not a child holding a דינר: a father would pick up a fallen coin. A ברייתא then supports רבא: clothes that are worn count as part of the person, but clothes that are only carried are a load. Next, the גמרא asks why a basket with a stone inside is not a בסיס לדבר האסור. It answers step by step: the basket is full of fruit, the fruit would be ruined if dumped, and the stone plugs a hole in the basket. Then רב חסדא limits moving impure תרומה with pure תרומה to when the pure is underneath. A ברייתא seems to refute him, but he answers that the משנה deals with needing the fruit itself (לצורך גופו) and the ברייתא with needing the spot (לצורך מקומו). רבא supports this reading from the coins-on-a-cushion clause. Finally, the גמרא asks why רבי יהודה lets one lift out nullified תרומה on שבת without counting it as fixing the food. It tries linking him to רבי אליעזר and then to רבי שמעון, rejects both, and settles on רבי שמעון בן אלעזר. It then asks whether רבי יהודה really holds that view, a question that continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Why only a stone? A coin should be the same
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why the משנה mentions a stone, since a דינר is also מוקצה. It then points out that רבא actually forbids the case of a דינר.
steps.simpleTranslation: Why does the משנה speak specifically about a stone? The same should be true even for a coin! So why did רבא say: They only taught this about a stone, but with a coin it is forbidden?
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה allows a person to pick up his child even though the child is holding a stone. The גמרא asks why a coin should be any different, and why רבא forbids it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A stone and a דינר are both מוקצה, so the reason that allows lifting the child seems to apply equally to both. Yet רבא draws a line between them. The גמרא wants to know what makes the coin different.

keyTerms.meaning: Why specifically this case? (asks why a particular example was chosen)
A coin; something valuable but מוקצה on שבת
They only taught this in the case of...

phrases.english: Why specifically a stone?
Even a coin should also be allowed!
Why then did Rava say:
They only taught this about a stone,
but a coin is forbidden!

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי אִירְיָא אֶבֶן, אֲפִילּוּ דִּינָר נָמֵי! אַלְּמָה אָמַר רָבָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the discussion of the משנה's case of lifting a child holding a stone
steps.kashyaTarget: רבא's distinction between a stone and a דינר
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Both objects are מוקצה, so there seems to be no reason to treat them differently

steps.title: A father would pick up a fallen coin but not a stone
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains that a coin is forbidden as a גזירה. If a coin falls, the father will pick it up, which is a real איסור of handling מוקצה.
steps.simpleTranslation: A stone, if it falls, the father will not come to pick it up. A coin, if it falls, the father will come to pick it up.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the difference is about human behavior. People don't care about a dropped stone, but they do care about a dropped coin.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Lifting the child with a coin is not forbidden on its own merits. חז"ל forbade it as a safeguard, because the father might grab the fallen coin and handle מוקצה directly. A stone has no value, so there is no such worry.

keyTerms.meaning: He will come to bring it (pick it up)

steps.whatToRemember: A child holding a stone may be lifted, but not a child holding a דינר, because a father would pick up a fallen coin.

phrases.english: A stone, if it falls —
his father will not come to bring it.
A coin, if it falls —
his father will come to bring it.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶבֶן, אִי נָפְלָה (לַהּ) — לָא אָתֵי אֲבוּהּ לְאֵיתוֹיֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 1
steps.terutzResolutionType: Rabbinic decree (גזירה) based on likely human behavior
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A stone and a coin should be treated the same, since both are מוקצה
steps.terutzMaskana: A coin is forbidden as a safeguard, because the father would pick it up if it fell

steps.title: A ברייתא supporting רבא: clothes carried versus clothes worn
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא teaches that carrying out folded clothes, sandals, or rings in the hand makes one חייב. Wearing them makes one פטור.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was taught in a ברייתא in support of רבא: One who carries out his clothes folded and resting on his shoulder, and his sandals and rings in his hand, is liable. If he was wearing them, he is exempt.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that supports רבא's earlier ruling. רבא held that something carried along with a person, but not worn in the normal way, is not counted as part of the person.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When clothing is worn normally, it becomes part of the person, so no הוצאה has happened. When the same clothing is carried on the shoulder or in the hand, it is an ordinary object being carried, so the person is חייב.

keyTerms.meaning: It was taught in a ברייתא in support of him
One who carries out (from a private domain to a public one)

steps.confusionAlert: The same objects can be חייב or פטור depending only on how they are carried. Wearing them makes them part of you. Holding them makes them a load.

phrases.english: It was taught in accordance with Rava:
One who carries out his clothes folded
and resting on his shoulder,
and his sandals and rings in his hand — is liable.
And if he was wearing them — he is exempt.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings outside support for רבא's earlier ruling on the daf
steps.raayaObject: רבא's ruling that items carried with a person, but not worn normally, are not counted as part of the person
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא about carrying clothes, sandals, and rings

steps.title: Carrying a person who is dressed versus a person holding his clothes
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא continues. Carrying out a person who is wearing his clothes is פטור. If the person holds those same clothes as they are, the one carrying him is חייב.
steps.simpleTranslation: One who carries out a person with his clothes on him, his sandals on his feet, and his rings on his hands is exempt. But if he carried them out as they are, he is liable.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא applies the same idea to carrying another person. This is the same kind of case רבא was talking about.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A living person "carries himself" (חי נושא את עצמו), and clothes he wears are part of him, so the carrier is פטור. If the clothes are just being held, they are not part of the person, so the carrier is חייב for them. This matches רבא exactly.

keyTerms.meaning: As they are (just held, not worn)

steps.whatToRemember: Only things worn in the normal way become part of the person. Anything merely held or hung on him is still a load, as רבא taught.

phrases.english: One who carries out a person with his clothes on him,
and his sandals on his feet,
and his rings on his hands — is exempt,
whereas if he carried them out as they are — he is liable.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Second half of the same ברייתא, applying the rule to carrying a person
steps.raayaObject: רבא's ruling about objects carried along with a person

steps.title: Why isn't the basket a base for the stone?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's case of a basket with a stone inside. It asks why the basket isn't a בסיס לדבר האסור, which would make it forbidden to move.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה says: a basket with a stone inside it may be moved. But why? The basket should be a base for a forbidden object!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves on to the משנה's second case and challenges it. A container holding מוקצה usually becomes forbidden to move as well.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally a container holding only מוקצה becomes a בסיס and takes on the same מוקצה status. So the משנה's permission to move the basket seems to contradict that rule.

keyTerms.meaning: A base for a forbidden (מוקצה) object, which itself becomes forbidden to move

phrases.english: A basket with the stone inside it.
But why?
Let the basket be
a base for a forbidden object!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns to the משנה and opens a new topic
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's permission to move a basket containing a stone
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A container of מוקצה becomes a בסיס לדבר האסור and should be forbidden to move

steps.title: The basket is full of fruit
steps.stepSummary: רבה בר בר חנה in the name of רבי יוחנן says the basket also holds fruit. That means it is a base for permitted things too.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה בר בר חנה said in the name of רבי יוחנן: Here we are dealing with a basket full of fruit.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the משנה's basket contains fruit as well as the stone. So it is not a base only for something forbidden.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since the basket holds both permitted fruit and the מוקצה stone, it is a base for both. The basket does not become מוקצה, so it may be moved for the sake of the fruit.

keyTerms.meaning: Here we are dealing with... (narrows the case)

phrases.english: Rabba bar bar Ḥana said
that Rabbi Yoḥanan said:
Here we are dealing with a basket full of fruit.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבָּה בַּר בַּר חָנָה אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן: הָכָא בְּכַלְכַּלָּה מְלֵאָה פֵּירוֹת עָסְקִינַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 5 by narrowing the case
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The basket holds only the stone, so it is a בסיס לדבר האסור
steps.terutzMaskana: The basket also holds fruit, so it is a base for permitted things as well

steps.title: Why not dump everything and carry the fruit by hand?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why he doesn't simply shake out the fruit and the stone and then pick up the fruit by hand. That way the stone is never moved.
steps.simpleTranslation: But let him throw out the fruit, throw out the stone, and take the fruit in his hands!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the answer. There seems to be an easy way to avoid moving the מוקצה stone at all.
steps.deeperAnalysis: One may not move מוקצה indirectly when there is a reasonable way to avoid it. Dumping the basket would separate the stone from the fruit, so carrying the stone seems unnecessary.

keyTerms.meaning: And let him throw them out

phrases.english: But let him throw out the fruit,
and throw out the stone,
and take the fruit in his hands!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer given in step 6
steps.kashyaTarget: The permission to move the stone together with the fruit
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: There is a simple way to avoid moving the מוקצה: empty the basket and carry the fruit alone

steps.title: The fruit would get dirty and ruined
steps.stepSummary: Using רבי אלעי's statement in the name of רב, the גמרא says the case involves fruit that gets dirty if thrown down. So dumping it is not a real option.
steps.simpleTranslation: As רבי אלעי said in the name of רב: it is talking about fruits that get dirty. Here too, it is talking about fruits that get dirty.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that dumping the basket would ruin the fruit. That is why he may carry the whole basket, stone and all.
steps.deeperAnalysis: חז"ל do not require a person to destroy his food in order to avoid moving מוקצה indirectly. The גמרא borrows רב's explanation from a different case and applies it here.

keyTerms.meaning: As רבי אלעי said in the name of רב
Fruits that get dirty or spoiled

steps.whatToRemember: At this stage, a basket holding a stone may be moved when it is also full of fruit that would be ruined if dumped out. Step 10 adds one more condition.

phrases.english: As Rabbi Elai said that Rav said:
with fruits that become soiled,
here too: with fruits that become soiled.

steps.triggerLanguage: כִּדְרַבִּי אִלְעַי אָמַר רַב: בְּפֵירוֹת הַמִּיטַּנְּפִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 7
steps.terutzResolutionType: Further narrowing of the case, using a parallel statement
steps.terutzHavaAmina: He could empty the basket and avoid moving the stone
steps.terutzMaskana: The fruit would get dirty and ruined, so he does not have to dump it

steps.title: Why not shake the stone out?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why the person doesn't just shake the basket so the stone can be tossed out, leaving only the fruit.
steps.simpleTranslation: But let him shake them out!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back again on the basket case. Even if dumping everything would dirty the fruit, he could shake the basket until the stone slides to one side and toss just the stone out.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 8 explained why he can't dump the fruit. This new challenge suggests a gentler option: remove only the stone, so the fruit never touches the ground. If that works, carrying the stone along with the basket would be unnecessary.

phrases.english: But let him shake them out!
phrases.notes: Shake the basket so the stone moves to one side and can be thrown out alone.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Follows up on the answer of step 8 with a new practical alternative.
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's permission to carry the basket with the stone inside, as explained in steps 6 and 8.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the stone can be removed by itself without harming the fruit, there is no need to move the stone at all.

steps.title: The stone plugs a hole in the basket
steps.stepSummary: רבא explains that the basket is broken and the stone is filling the hole, so removing it would spill the fruit.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חייא בר אשי said in the name of רבא: Here we are dealing with a broken basket, where the stone itself serves as a wall of the basket.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא answers that the basket has a hole, and the stone is blocking it. Taking the stone out would let the fruit fall through, so the stone has to stay.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once the stone works as part of the basket's wall, it is no longer just a forbidden object sitting inside. It is serving the basket. That is why it can be moved along with the basket and the fruit.
steps.whatToRemember: The basket-with-stone case ends with three answers: the basket holds fruit too, the fruit would get dirty if dumped, and the stone plugs a hole in the basket.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב חִיָּיא בַּר אָשֵׁי אָמַר רָבָא:
phrases.english: Rav Hiyya bar Ashi said that Rava said:
Here we are dealing with a broken basket,
where the stone itself becomes a wall of the basket.
phrases.notes: The stone blocks the hole, so taking it out would spill the fruit.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 9.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Narrowing the case (אוקימתא) to a specific situation
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The stone is a separate object that could easily be removed alone.
steps.terutzMaskana: The stone is part of the basket's structure, so removing it is not a real option.

steps.title: רב חסדא limits the תרומה case
steps.stepSummary: On the משנה's case of moving impure תרומה with pure תרומה, רב חסדא says this is allowed only when the pure is on the bottom.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: 'One may move תרומה, etc.' רב חסדא said: They only taught this when the pure is on the bottom and the impure is on top. But if the pure is on top and the impure on the bottom, he takes the pure and leaves the impure.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves on to the next case in the משנה. רב חסדא says you may move impure תרומה along with pure תרומה only when the impure is lying on top and is in the way.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the pure fruit is on top, you can simply take it and leave the impure fruit untouched, so there is no reason to move the forbidden item. Only when the impure is on top, blocking the pure, is it allowed to move them together.

keyTerms.meaning: impure תרומה, which may not be eaten and is מוקצה on שבת
they only taught this in a case of

steps.confusionAlert: Why is impure תרומה forbidden to move? A כהן may not eat it, and it cannot be burned on שבת, so on שבת it has no use and counts as מוקצה.

phrases.english: 'One may move (impure) teruma, etc.'
Rav Hisda said:
They only taught this when the pure is on the bottom
and the impure is on top.
But if the pure is on top and the impure on the bottom —
he takes the pure
and leaves the impure.

steps.triggerLanguage: מְטַלְטְלִין תְּרוּמָה וְכוּ׳ אָמַר רַב חִסְדָּא לֹא שָׁנוּ אֶלָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic: the next case in the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Impure תרומה may be moved together with pure תרומה only when the impure is on top. When the pure is on top, he takes only the pure.

steps.title: Why not dump the impure fruit?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why, even when the pure is underneath, he doesn't just dump everything and pick up the pure fruit.
steps.simpleTranslation: And even when the pure is on the bottom, let him throw them down and pick up (the pure)!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רב חסדא's permitted case too. Even when the impure is on top, he could pour everything out and pick up only the pure fruit by hand.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is the same kind of challenge as step 7. If there is a way to get the pure fruit without carrying the impure, then moving the impure should never be allowed.

phrases.english: And when the pure is on the bottom as well,
let him throw them down and pick them up!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכִי טְהוֹרָה לְמַטָּה נָמֵי לִישְׁדִּינְהוּ וְלִינְקְטִינְהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the case that רב חסדא permitted.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב חסדא's permitted case (pure below, impure above).
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Dumping everything and picking up the pure would avoid moving the impure at all.

steps.title: The fruit would get dirty
steps.stepSummary: Using רבי אלעי's statement in the name of רב, the גמרא answers that the case involves fruit that gets ruined if thrown down.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אלעי said in the name of רב: We are dealing with fruits that get dirty.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the same answer it gave in step 8. Dumping would ruin the fruit, so it is not a real option.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since dumping would spoil the pure fruit, the only practical way to get it is to move the impure fruit along with it. This keeps רב חסדא's ruling standing for now.

keyTerms.meaning: fruits that get dirty and ruined

phrases.english: Rabbi Elai said that Rav said:
We are dealing with fruits that get dirty.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 12, reusing the answer from step 8.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Narrowing the case (אוקימתא) to a specific situation
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The fruit could be dumped with no harm.
steps.terutzMaskana: The fruit would be ruined, so dumping it is not an option.

steps.title: A ברייתא permits either order
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that allows moving impure תרומה with pure, whichever one is on top.
steps.simpleTranslation: They challenged: One may move impure תרומה with pure and with חולין, whether the pure is on top and the impure below, or the impure is on top and the pure below.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes a ברייתא that seems to contradict רב חסדא directly.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב חסדא said that when the pure is on top, you must take only the pure. The ברייתא says it is allowed either way, including when the pure is on top. That is exactly the case רב חסדא forbade.

phrases.english: They raised an objection:
One may move impure teruma
with the pure and with the non-sacred produce,
whether the pure is on top and the impure below,
or the impure is on top and the pure below,

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks רב חסדא's statement from step 11 using a ברייתא.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב חסדא's limitation (allowed only when the pure is on the bottom).
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא explicitly permits the case of pure on top, which רב חסדא forbade.

steps.title: The ברייתא seems to refute רב חסדא
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא states that the ברייתא appears to be a full refutation of רב חסדא. The next step shows how רב חסדא answers it.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is a refutation of רב חסדא!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא sharpens the challenge from step 14: as things stand, the ברייתא seems to contradict רב חסדא outright. This sets up the next step, where רב חסדא defends himself.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא explicitly permits the case of pure on top, which רב חסדא forbade, so it seems to refute him. Here, though, the גמרא answers this in step 16 by explaining the משנה and the ברייתא as different cases, so רב חסדא's limit survives for the case where one needs the fruit itself.
steps.whatToRemember: The ברייתא seems to refute רב חסדא, but this is not the final word. In step 16 רב חסדא answers that the משנה and the ברייתא describe different cases.
steps.whyThisMatters: The word תיובתא usually signals a final refutation. Here, though, the גמרא goes on to show that רב חסדא can answer it, so his limit still holds when one needs the fruit itself (לצורך גופו).

phrases.english: A refutation of Rav Hisda!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the challenge of step 14 by stating that it seems to refute רב חסדא. Step 16 answers it.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Not final. The challenge stands only until step 16, where רב חסדא splits the cases: the משנה is לצורך גופו and the ברייתא is לצורך מקומו.

steps.title: רב חסדא answers by splitting the cases: the fruit itself versus the space
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא explains that the משנה deals with someone who needs the fruit itself (לצורך גופו). The ברייתא deals with someone who needs the basket's place (לצורך מקומו). So the two sources do not contradict each other.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חסדא can say to you: The משנה is talking about when he needs the object itself. The ברייתא is talking about when he needs its place.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows that רב חסדא is not refuted after all. The משנה and the ברייתא are simply talking about two different situations.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When a person wants to eat the pure fruit (לצורך גופו), רב חסדא's limit applies: he may move the basket only if the pure fruit is on the bottom. When he just needs to clear the spot (לצורך מקומו), he may move the basket no matter which fruit is on top, and that is the case the ברייתא describes. The challenge from step 14 goes away because the two sources are not discussing the same case.

keyTerms.meaning: For the need of the object itself, meaning he wants to use the item (here, to eat the fruit)
For the need of its place, meaning he wants the spot where the item is sitting
A teaching from the time of the משנה that was not included in the משנה
"He can say to you": introduces how a challenged אמורא would defend himself

steps.confusionAlert: Step 15 seemed to end with רב חסדא refuted, but this step shows he can defend himself. Read step 15 as the strong challenge and this step as the way out.
steps.whyThisMatters: The difference between לצורך גופו and לצורך מקומו is a central idea in the laws of מוקצה across all of שבת. Moving something for its place is often more lenient.

phrases.english: Rav Chisda can say to you:
The Mishnah is for the need of the object itself (he wants the fruit),
the baraita is for the need of its place (he wants the spot cleared).

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Defends רב חסדא against the refutation raised from the ברייתא in steps 14-15.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the cases (אוקימתא): the two sources describe different purposes for moving the basket.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא allows moving the basket in any arrangement, which seems to directly contradict רב חסדא's limit.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ברייתא is about לצורך מקומו and רב חסדא's limit is about לצורך גופו, so there is no contradiction.

steps.title: What forced רב חסדא to read the משנה this way?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why רב חסדא had to say that the משנה is specifically about needing the fruit itself.
steps.simpleTranslation: What pressured רב חסדא to establish the משנה as talking about the need of the object itself?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a clarifying question about רב חסדא's reading of the משנה. This sets up the next step, where רבא gives the reason.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה does not say anything about "for the fruit itself." The גמרא wants to know what in the text pushes us to limit the משנה to that case instead of reading it as covering every case.

keyTerms.meaning: "What pressured him?": what forced this reading?
To establish, meaning to set a source in a specific case

phrases.english: What pressured Rav Chisda
to establish the Mishnah as for the need of the object itself?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions the basis of the אוקימתא just given in step 16.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What textual reason forces the משנה to be limited to לצורך גופו?

steps.title: רבא proves the reading from the coins-on-a-cushion case
steps.stepSummary: רבא says the משנה itself supports רב חסדא. The next clause, about shaking coins off a cushion, is explained by רבי יוחנן as לצורך גופו. Since the later clause is לצורך גופו, the earlier clause is too.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: The משנה is precise in line with him. It teaches in the later part: coins on a cushion, he shakes the cushion and they fall off. And רבה בר בר חנה said in the name of רבי יוחנן: They taught this only for the need of the cushion itself. But for the need of its place, he moves it while the coins are still on it. And since the later part is for the need of the object itself, the first part is also for the need of the object itself.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא answers the question from step 17. He shows from the very next case in the משנה that the whole section is about needing the object itself.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה requires shaking the coins off the cushion, and רבי יוחנן limits that to when he needs the cushion itself. If he only needs the spot, he may move the cushion with the coins still on it. Because the later case (סיפא) is clearly about לצורך גופו, it makes sense that the earlier case (רישא) about the תרומה basket is also about לצורך גופו.

keyTerms.meaning: Is precise: the wording of the source supports this reading
The later clause of a משנה
The first clause of a משנה
He shakes (the cushion, so the מוקצה coins fall off)
"They taught this only...": limits a ruling to a specific case

steps.whatToRemember: רב חסדא survives. The משנה (לצורך גופו) and the ברייתא (לצורך מקומו) are different cases, and the coins-on-a-cushion clause shows the משנה is about לצורך גופו.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is a classic way the גמרא reads a משנה: the רישא and סיפא are assumed to be talking about the same kind of case.

phrases.english: Rava said:
The Mishnah is precise in line with him (Rav Chisda),
since it teaches in the later clause:
Coins that are on a cushion:
he shakes the cushion and they fall off.
And Rabbah bar bar Chana said
in the name of Rabbi Yochanan:
They taught this only for the need of the object itself,
but for the need of its place,
he moves it while they (the coins) are still on it.
And since the later clause is for the need of the object itself,
the first clause is also for the need of the object itself.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 17 by bringing support from the סיפא of the משנה.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The סיפא (coins on a cushion) is לצורך גופו according to רבי יוחנן, so the רישא must be לצורך גופו as well.
steps.raayaObject: רב חסדא's reading of the משנה as לצורך גופו
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה's case of coins on a cushion, as explained by רבה בר בר חנה in the name of רבי יוחנן

steps.title: Why may one lift out the nullified תרומה on שבת?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes רבי יהודה's ruling in the משנה that one may even lift out nullified תרומה. It then asks why this is allowed, since doing so seems to fix the food so it can be eaten.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהודה says: One may even lift out, etc. But why? He is fixing (the food)!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new topic. It quotes the next ruling in the משנה and challenges it as a forbidden act of fixing (מתקן) on שבת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The case is תרומה that fell into 100 parts of regular food and became nullified (בטלה). Lifting out one measure of the mixture makes the rest clearly permitted to a non-כהן. Since the חכמים forbade fixing or preparing food for use on שבת, the גמרא asks how רבי יהודה can allow it.

keyTerms.meaning: One lifts out (a measure of תרומה from the mixture)
Fixing, meaning making something fit for use, which the חכמים forbade on שבת
"Etc.": the rest of the quoted משנה

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר: אַף מַעֲלִין וְכוּ׳.
phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda says: One may even lift out, etc.
But why?!
He is fixing (the food)!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the topic of moving the basket and starts a new discussion on the next clause of the משנה.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יהודה's ruling in the משנה that one may lift out nullified תרומה on שבת
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Lifting out the תרומה makes the mixture usable, which is the forbidden act of מתקן on שבת.

steps.title: רבי יהודה follows רבי אליעזר: the תרומה stays as it is
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers the question from step 19. רבי יהודה agrees with רבי אליעזר, who holds that תרומה inside a mixture is treated as if it is still there, separate. So lifting it out is not fixing the food.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהודה holds like רבי אליעזר, who said: the תרומה is considered as if it is lying there in its original form.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question of why רבי יהודה lets you lift out the תרומה on שבת. It says he follows רבי אליעזר's idea that the תרומה never really mixed in.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The problem was that lifting out the תרומה seems to turn forbidden food into permitted food, and that is 'fixing' (מתקן). If the original תרומה is treated as still sitting there unmixed, then the leftover food was never truly forbidden. Lifting out the תרומה just removes what is already separate, so nothing gets fixed.

keyTerms.meaning: The תרומה is considered as lying in its original form, not truly mixed in
In its original state, as it is

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה כְּרַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר סְבִירָא לֵיהּ,
phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda holds like Rabbi Eliezer,
who said: the terumah is regarded as lying there in its original state.
phrases.notes: So removing a measure of it counts as removing the actual תרומה. It does not 'repair' the mixture.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה כְּרַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר סְבִירָא לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 19 against רבי יהודה.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Linking רבי יהודה to an earlier תנא's view that changes how the act is understood
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Lifting out the תרומה turns forbidden food into permitted food, so it is מתקן on שבת.
steps.terutzMaskana: If the תרומה stays 'בעינה', lifting it out only removes the תרומה itself. Nothing is fixed.

steps.title: The משנה showing רבי אליעזר's view
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes a משנה where רבי אליעזר treats part of a mixture as if it could be pure תרומה. The חכמים say it only counts by proportion.
steps.simpleTranslation: As we learned in a משנה: A סאה of תרומה fell into less than 100 סאה of regular food, so the whole thing became a forbidden mixture (מדומע). Then a סאה from that mixture fell into a different pile. רבי אליעזר says: it makes the new pile a forbidden mixture, as if it were definite תרומה. The חכמים say: the mixture only makes the new pile forbidden according to its proportion of תרומה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings the source showing that רבי אליעזר holds 'the תרומה stays as it is.'
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אליעזר worries that the exact סאה that fell out of the first mixture might be the original, unmixed תרומה. So he treats it like full תרומה. The חכמים say each part of the mixture holds only its share of תרומה, so only that small amount counts. רבי אליעזר's view matches the idea that the תרומה never truly blended in.

keyTerms.meaning: A forbidden mixture of תרומה and regular food

steps.confusionAlert: Do not confuse this case with the rule of 1 in 101. Here the תרומה fell into LESS than 100, so it was never nullified. That is why the mixture became forbidden.

phrases.english: As we learned in a Mishnah: a se'ah of terumah
that fell into less than one hundred, and they became a forbidden mixture,
and some of the mixture fell into another place,

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר אוֹמֵר: מְדַמַּעַת כִּתְרוּמַת וַדַּאי.
phrases.english: Rabbi Eliezer says: it makes it a forbidden mixture like definite terumah.
And the Sages say:

phrases.aramaic: אֵין הַמְדוּמָּע מְדַמֵּעַ אֶלָּא לְפִי חֶשְׁבּוֹן.
phrases.english: the mixture only makes a forbidden mixture according to proportion.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the source for the view of רבי אליעזר cited in step 20.
steps.raayaObject: That רבי אליעזר holds תרומה בעינה מחתא
steps.raayaSupportSource: משנה in תרומות about a סאה from a מדומע falling into another pile

steps.title: רבי אליעזר was only strict, not lenient
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the link. רבי אליעזר used this idea only to be strict. It does not follow that he would use it to be lenient and permit the leftover food.
steps.simpleTranslation: Say that you heard him use this idea to be strict. Did you hear him use it to be lenient?!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the answer from step 20. It says רבי אליעזר's ruling cannot support a lenient ruling for רבי יהודה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the משנה, רבי אליעזר only worried that the תרומה MIGHT not have mixed in, so he forbade the second pile out of doubt. That is a strict ruling. He never said for sure that the תרומה stays separate. So we cannot use his view to say that lifting out תרומה is NOT fixing. That would be a lenient use.

keyTerms.meaning: Say that you heard him (rule this way)

steps.whyThisMatters: This is a common move in the גמרא: a view stated as a strict concern from doubt cannot automatically be used to make a lenient ruling.

phrases.english: Say that you heard him (rule this way) to be stringent,
to be lenient, did you hear him?!

steps.triggerLanguage: אֵימַר דְּשָׁמְעַתְּ לֵיהּ לְחוּמְרָא, לְקוּלָּא מִי שָׁמְעַתְּ לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the answer of step 20 by limiting the reach of the source in step 21.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The link between רבי יהודה's lenient ruling and רבי אליעזר's view
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: רבי אליעזר's ruling is a strict ruling based on doubt. It cannot prove a lenient rule that removing תרומה is not fixing.

steps.title: A new source: רבי יהודה follows רבי שמעון
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests that רבי יהודה follows רבי שמעון, who permits a mixture even after a second סאה of תרומה falls in.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, רבי יהודה said his ruling following רבי שמעון. As we learned in a משנה: one סאה of תרומה fell into one hundred סאה of regular food. Before the person could lift it out, another סאה fell in. The mixture is forbidden. But רבי שמעון permits it.
steps.whatsHappening: The רבי אליעזר answer was rejected in the last step, so the גמרא tries a new answer to the question from step 19. It suggests that רבי יהודה agrees with רבי שמעון.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The idea is that רבי שמעון sees the first סאה as if it is still sitting there on its own, so it does not join with the second סאה. Unlike רבי אליעזר, he uses this idea to be lenient. If the תרומה is already seen as separate, then lifting it out does not fix the food.

keyTerms.meaning: To lift out the measure of תרומה from the mixture
As we learned in a משנה

phrases.english: Rather, he said it following Rabbi Shimon,
as we learned in a Mishnah:
A se'a of teruma that fell into one hundred se'a,
phrases.notes: One part in 100 would normally be nullified.

phrases.english: and he did not manage to lift it out
before another se'a fell in
— this mixture is forbidden.
phrases.notes: Now there are 2 parts of תרומה to 100 parts of regular food.

phrases.english: And Rabbi Shimon permits it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the רבי אליעזר answer, which step 22 rejected, with a new source.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Identifying a different תנא whose view supports רבי יהודה
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Lifting the nullified תרומה fixes the food, so it should be forbidden on שבת.
steps.terutzMaskana: רבי שמעון treats the fallen תרומה as standing on its own, even to be lenient. So lifting it out is not fixing the food.

steps.title: רבי שמעון's reason may be different
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the link. The argument may really be about whether the two סאה count as falling at the same time.
steps.simpleTranslation: How do you know? Maybe they argue about something else. The first תנא holds that even though the two fell one after the other, it is as if they fell together. Then each one fell into only fifty, which is not enough. רבי שמעון holds that the first one was already nullified in one hundred. The second one is then nullified in one hundred and one.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on step 23. It shows that the argument between the תנא קמא and רבי שמעון can be explained in a way that has nothing to do with lifting out תרומה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here the question is timing. Does the second סאה join the first one, so that two סאה are in only one hundred? Or was the first סאה already nullified and absorbed? On this reading, רבי שמעון never says the תרומה is seen as standing apart, so the proof for רבי יהודה falls away.

keyTerms.meaning: And from where do you know this? (opens a rejection)

steps.confusionAlert: In this reading רבי שמעון permits the mixture because the first סאה became part of the regular food. That adds a סאה to the total, making 101. It is NOT because the תרומה is seen as standing apart, which is the opposite of step 23's idea.

phrases.english: And from where do you know this?
Perhaps there they argue about this:
that the first tanna holds

phrases.aramaic: אַף עַל גַּב דְּנָפְלוּ בָּזֶה אַחַר זֶה
phrases.english: even though they fell one after the other
— it is as if they fell at the same time.
So this one fell into fifty,
and that one fell into fifty.
phrases.notes: Fifty is not enough to nullify, so the mixture is forbidden.

phrases.english: And Rabbi Shimon holds:
The first one was already nullified in one hundred,
and this one will be nullified in one hundred and one.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the source proposed in step 23.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects only the link between רבי שמעון and רבי יהודה. רבי שמעון's ruling itself stays.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The argument can be explained as being about timing and joining, not about seeing the תרומה as standing apart.

steps.title: A third source: רבי שמעון בן אלעזר
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests that רבי יהודה follows רבי שמעון בן אלעזר, who says one can eat from the mixture without lifting anything out.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, רבי יהודה said his ruling following רבי שמעון בן אלעזר. As taught in a ברייתא, רבי שמעון בן אלעזר says: a person sets his eyes on one side of the mixture and eats from the other side.
steps.whatsHappening: Since the רבי שמעון link was rejected, the גמרא offers a third answer. רבי יהודה follows רבי שמעון בן אלעזר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי שמעון בן אלעזר says you do not need to physically take out the סאה first. You only need to have in mind which part you will remove, and then you can already eat from another part. So the food is already edible, and lifting the תרומה out on שבת does not fix it.

keyTerms.meaning: As was taught in a ברייתא
Sets his eyes on it, meaning he picks a part in his mind

steps.whyThisMatters: This answer works because it removes the problem at its root. If the food can be eaten even without lifting, then lifting cannot count as fixing it.

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא: הוּא דְּאָמַר כְּרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן אֶלְעָזָר.
phrases.english: Rather, he said it following Rabbi Shimon ben Elazar.
As it was taught in a baraita:
Rabbi Shimon ben Elazar says:
He sets his eyes on this side,
phrases.notes: He decides in his mind that the תרומה will come from here.

phrases.english: and eats from the other side.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא: הוּא דְּאָמַר כְּרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן אֶלְעָזָר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the רבי שמעון answer, which step 24 rejected.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Identifying a different תנא whose view supports רבי יהודה
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Lifting out the סאה is what makes the mixture edible, so it fixes the food.
steps.terutzMaskana: The mixture can be eaten just by choosing a part in one's mind, so lifting it out does not fix anything.

steps.title: Does רבי יהודה really agree with רבי שמעון בן אלעזר?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא questions whether רבי יהודה actually holds like רבי שמעון בן אלעזר.
steps.simpleTranslation: And does רבי יהודה really agree with him?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the answer from step 25. This short line sets up the next move, where the גמרא will show the problem.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question suggests that somewhere else רבי יהודה may hold a different view about choosing a part in one's mind. If so, he cannot be relying on רבי שמעון בן אלעזר here. The proof will come next.

keyTerms.meaning: And does he really agree with him? (a challenging question)

phrases.english: And does he really hold like him?
phrases.notes: Does רבי יהודה hold like רבי שמעון בן אלעזר?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the source proposed in step 25.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that רבי יהודה follows רבי שמעון בן אלעזר
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: This implies that רבי יהודה's known views elsewhere may conflict with רבי שמעון בן אלעזר. The details come on the next amud.
